notes.summary: Partial P15.2 theorem for arbitrary pseudoeffective zero-volume classes, without a fibration: bounded actual type has degree d<n, mixed vanishing, a positive raw-mass operator on X, sufficient perturbation convergence and a class-dependent bounded primitive. Full-form dependence remains.
notes.detailedSummary: For actual theta-psh psi, define M_k=int<T_psi^k>omega^(n-k), M_0=int omega^n, and d=max{k:M_k>0}. The actual-mass upper bound by perturbed class volume proves d<n. Positive-form comparison makes d independent of the auxiliary form. DDNL mixed mass equality and positivity give higher-degree mixed current vanishing. The operator <T_u^d>omega^(n-d) has mass M_d and carrier X of dimension n. Admissible signed IBP proves rescaled operator convergence when sup|u_epsilon-u|=o(epsilon). Its bounded primitive has a cocycle, concavity and representative independence within the auxiliary class. Exact coefficients give an energy limit requiring only uniform distance tending to zero, including arbitrary representatives of converging Kähler classes. This does not establish unrestricted perturbation independence, a minimum-reference characterization or an intrinsic lower-dimensional carrier.
notes.text:
This is a narrower theorem in an unverified mathematical draft, addressing only P15.2. The unchanged original atom is not claimed solved.

Ambient hypotheses: X is connected, smooth, compact Kähler of complex dimension n>=1; alpha is pseudoeffective with vol(alpha)=0; theta is a smooth representative; psi is an actual theta-psh function not identically minus infinity; omega is a Kähler form. Use dc=i(barpartial-partial)/(4pi), ddc=i partial barpartial/(2pi). Write T_u=theta+ddc u and P=T_psi. The bounded domain C_psi consists of theta-psh u satisfying psi-C<=u<=psi+C as extended-valued functions. Thus it retains actual bounded singularity type, not I-equivalence, and the polar loci agree. Comparing only on an intersection of finite loci would be insufficient.

The standard foundations used are stated and applied explicitly. BEGZ, Monge–Ampère equations in big cohomology classes, Acta Math.205(2010),199–262, Propositions1.4,1.6 and Theorem1.8, gives finite, closed, positive, symmetric, positive-multilinear and plurifine-local nonpluripolar products of closed positive (1,1) currents on compact Kähler X, with no pluripolar mass. DDNL, Monotonicity of nonpluripolar products and complex Monge–Ampère equations with prescribed singularity, Anal.PDE11(2018),2049–2087, Proposition2.1, gives equality of top mixed masses when each pair of potentials has the same bounded singularity type, for pseudoeffective backgrounds. Its Theorem2.4 says making every factor more singular cannot increase that mass. Lower-degree applications fill the remaining slots with smooth Kähler forms and zero potentials. BEGZ Section1.4 and Definition1.17 provide a minimal-singularity current Q_min in a big class beta whose top mass is vol(beta), and define the pseudoeffective boundary volume by lim_{epsilon down0}vol(alpha+epsilon[omega]). DDNL monotonicity therefore bounds every actual top mass in beta by vol(beta). Equality for an arbitrary actual current is never asserted.

The signed IBP foundation is Vu, Convexity of the class of currents with finite relative energy, arXiv:2005.13241v3, Lemmas2.5,2.6 and Theorem2.7. For closed positive (n-1,n-1) R and bounded R-admissible dsh differences v,w, it gives integral w<ddc v dotwedge R>=integral v<ddc w dotwedge R>=-integral<dw wedge dc v dotwedge R>. The v=w gradient is positive and finite. Admissibility requires the polar loci of quasi-psh representatives to have no R mass. Here every R is a nonpluripolar product times smooth positive forms, or smooth, so every bounded difference used is admissible. Relative signed insertions coincide with differences of ordinary finite nonpluripolar products by local cutoffs and positive multilinearity; association is Vu Proposition2.1(iii).

Conventions are converted consistently. DDNL uses i partial barpartial, so its potential corresponding to ours is u/(2pi). Vu uses dc_s=2dc and ddc_s=2ddc; source potential u/2 represents the same actual current. Its gradient of v/2 is half our gradient of v. Both sides of its IBP become half our formula, so multiplying by two gives the stated identity. The correct gradient identity is (1/2)ddc(v^2)-v ddc v. Vu v3 Eq(2.3) prints this correctly; repeated page6 and page11 formulas omit the half. Those literal defects are preserved in the dossier. With a=phi_1,k+rho and b=phi_2,k+rho, the correct local expansion is ddc(a^2)+ddc(b^2)-(1/2)ddc((a+b)^2)-v_k(ddc phi_1,k-ddc phi_2,k), wedged with R. The squares are bounded psh locally after positivity adjustment, so plurifine locality applies. The intrinsic gradient is positive and its mass is at most 2||v_k|| integral kappa R by Stokes. For the cutoff tending to1 off a locally complete pluripolar set not charged by R, Vu Theorem2.2 gives separately ddc(chi_k^2)R->0 and chi_k ddc chi_k R->0. A fixed strictly psh rho makes chi_k+rho psh and increasing; square/product expansions against fixed rho give these two limits. The corrected half-factor therefore still gives zero cutoff-gradient limit, and Cauchy–Schwarz kills the IBP boundary terms. The incorrect printed gradient expansions are not used. These results are scoped standard foundations, not newly reconstructed literature theorems.

Define M_k=integral<P^k>omega^(n-k), with <P^0>=1, and d=max{k:M_k>0}. M_0>0. Positive multilinearity gives integral<(P+epsilon omega)^n>=sum_k C(n,k)epsilon^(n-k)M_k<=vol(alpha+epsilon[omega])->0. The perturbed class is big because P+epsilon omega>=epsilon omega. Hence M_n=0 and d<n. If c omega<=eta<=C omega, positivity gives c^(n-k)M_k(omega)<=M_k(eta)<=C^(n-k)M_k(omega). Therefore positivity of every M_k, and d, is independent of the Kähler form.

For u_1,...,u_k in C_psi, DDNL mixed equality gives integral<T_u1 ... T_uk>omega^(n-k)=M_k. For k>d this is zero. A positive current with zero Kähler trace mass is zero: locally its measure coefficients are controlled by its positive trace. Thus higher-degree mixed products vanish as currents. Monotonicity gives the same vanishing for factors more singular than psi. Bounded-equivalent anchor changes preserve d and M_k. Closedness makes each M_k depend only on [omega].

Define the actual product current A(u)=<T_u^d>, of bidegree(d,d), and mu_(u,omega)=A(u)omega^(n-d). This is a positive nonpluripolar measure of raw mass M_d>0 on geometric carrier X of dimension n. Bidegree d does not construct a geometric d-fold. For fixed u, the exact expansion is
<(T_u+epsilon omega)^n>/(C(n,d)epsilon^(n-d))=mu_(u,omega)+sum_{k<d}(C(n,k)/C(n,d))epsilon^(d-k)<T_u^k>omega^(n-k).
The positive remainder has mass O(epsilon). For d=0 it is absent and the equality with omega^n is exact.

For u_epsilon in PSH(X,theta+epsilon omega) of the same bounded type, let delta=sup|u_epsilon-u| off the common polar locus, S=theta+epsilon omega+ddc u_epsilon, A=T_u+epsilon omega, h=u_epsilon-u, and R_j=<S^j A^(n-1-j)>. These are closed positive degree(n-1,n-1) currents; for n=1 the degree-zero current is1. Factorization and admissible IBP against real smooth f give integral f(<S^n>-<A^n>)=sum_j integral h ddc f R_j. Choose -C_f omega<=ddc f<=C_f omega. DDNL mixed equality gives integral omega R_j=integral omega<(P+epsilon omega)^(n-1)>=sum_{k<=d}C(n-1,k)epsilon^(n-1-k)M_k=O(epsilon^(n-d-1)). The rescaled error is therefore at most constant_f delta/epsilon. Uniform actual-mass bounds and density of smooth tests prove weak measure convergence if delta=o(epsilon). Smooth convergence omega_epsilon->omega>0 supplies uniform comparison constants and convergence of the leading current pairing, giving the same result. No rate-free assertion or optimality theorem is claimed.

For the bounded primitive define L_u(v)=integral v<T_u^d>omega^(n-d). On any fixed finite-dimensional convex hull of bounded-type potentials its coefficients are finite polynomials. For d>=1, D_a L_u(b)=d integral b<ddc a T_u^(d-1)>omega^(n-d), symmetric in a,b by admissible IBP. For d=0 the derivative is zero. Hence this polynomial one-form is closed. Its segment integral from psi to u, using integral_0^1 C(d,a)t^a(1-t)^(d-a)dt=1/(d+1), is
E_(psi,[omega])(u)=1/(d+1)sum_{a=0}^d integral(u-psi)<T_u^a P^(d-a)>omega^(n-d).
Ordinary Stokes on a triangle gives the exact cocycle E_psi(v)-E_psi(u)=E_u(v). For segments and C^1 paths in such a finite-dimensional hull, E'=integral dotu mu_u. Positivity and fixed segment mass give monotonicity, |E(v)-E(u)|<=M_d||v-u||, and E(u+c)=E(u)+cM_d. For d>=1 the segment second derivative is -d integral<dh dc h dotwedge(<T_ut^(d-1)>omega^(n-d))><=0, using the positive admissible gradient. For d=0 E=integral(u-psi)omega^n is affine. Arbitrary unbounded or discontinuous velocities are not included.

For cohomologous Kähler omega'=omega+ddc g, a real smooth g is supplied by the compact-Kähler ddc lemma: a smooth real closed cohomologically zero (1,1) form is ddc of a smooth real function. Citation: Deligne–Griffiths–Morgan–Sullivan, Real homotopy theory of Kähler manifolds, Invent.Math.29(1975),245–274, Section5; the global-potential consequence also appears in BEGZ Section1.3. All hypotheses apply to our smooth difference. Expand omega'^(n-d)-omega^(n-d)=ddc g sum_r omega'^r omega^(n-d-1-r). For each d-fold mixed Q, the current R=Q omega'^r omega^(n-d-1-r) is closed positive of degree n-1 and admissible. IBP transfers integral(u-psi)ddc g R to integral g<ddc(u-psi)R>. The latter is a difference of two (d+1)-fold same-type products, each zero. This proves representative independence of E, including d=0, but not of mu. Replacing theta by theta+ddc g and u,psi by u-g,psi-g preserves all currents and differences.

Put E^k=1/(k+1)sum_{j<=k}integral(u-psi)<T_u^jP^(k-j)>omega^(n-k), k<=d. Its magnitude is at most ||u-psi||M_k. The unnormalized positive-epsilon relative n-energy obeys the exact identity E^n_(psi,theta+epsilon omega)(u)=sum_{k<=d}C(n,k)epsilon^(n-k)E^k. Indeed sum_a C(a,j)C(n-a,k-j)=C(n+1,k+1), by counting a (k+1)-element subset according to its (j+1)-st member. Higher T-degree terms vanish. The leading coefficient is C(n,d)E^d. The positive-background cocycle and monotonicity give |E^n(u_epsilon)-E^n(u)|<=delta m_epsilon, with the ACTUAL anchor mass m_epsilon=sum_{k<=d}C(n,k)epsilon^(n-k)M_k. Thus the rescaled energy limit needs only delta->0.

For arbitrary Kähler representatives omega_epsilon with [omega_epsilon]->lambda Kähler, closedness makes M_k a continuous cohomological polynomial, uniformly bounded near lambda. The lower energy coefficients are bounded by ||u-psi||M_k and vanish after rescaling. Choose a fixed positive representative sigma_0 of lambda and smooth representatives beta_i of a finite cohomology basis. Locally sigma_0+sum b_i beta_i remains Kähler. Representative independence identifies E^d with a continuous polynomial in b_i, proving its limit E_(psi,lambda)(u). Uniformly bounded rescaled actual masses also handle delta->0. This is an energy assertion only; it gives neither representative independence of the entire positive-epsilon energy nor a form-free operator limit.

notes.summary: The actual operator extends to more-singular degree-d relative full-mass currents and is continuous under decreasing full-mass sequences. A genuine unbounded finite-energy example is given; the general unbounded energy cocycle and perturbation limits remain unresolved.
notes.detailedSummary: For u<=psi+C with int<T_u^d>omega^(n-d)=M_d, the operator of max(u,psi-j) converges to the actual operator. Mixed monotonicity gives equal intermediate masses. Vu Lemma4.1(i), applied with a constant smooth relative current, implies every weak cluster point dominates the actual product; equal masses force equality. This also proves decreasing full-mass continuity and independence of such decreasing majorants. Vu's linear joint finite-energy domain is identified and contains an explicit unbounded logarithmic-power example. Weighted truncation-value continuity, unbounded numerical cocycles and lower-degree perturbative integrability are not claimed.
notes.text:
Use n1's degree d, reference P, mixed monotonicity and mass M_d, with fixed full Kähler form omega. This proves an operator extension, not a general unbounded energy theorem.

Allow theta-psh u<=psi+C with integral<T_u^d>omega^(n-d)=M_d. Normalize u<=psi by a constant. If u<=v_i<=psi, DDNL Theorem2.4 places the degree-d mixed mass of the v_i between the equal pure masses of u and psi, so it equals M_d. In particular u_j=max(u,psi-j) is theta-psh, of bounded type [psi], decreases to u, and has mass M_d.

The additional standard foundation is Vu, Relative non-pluripolar product of currents, arXiv:2004.11111v1, Lemma4.1(i): for local psh p_i^l>=p_i converging in L1_loc, and closed positive R_l->R satisfying Condition(*), the relative products have lower-semicontinuous integrals against compactly supported smooth weakly positive test forms. Condition(*) requires locally uniformly bounded masses and the specified vanishing for decreasing psh sequences converging to bounded psh functions; the source explicitly lists constant sequences as examples. Here R_l=R=omega^(n-d) is smooth and constant, so the condition follows from decreasing Bedford–Taylor convergence. Its relative product equals the ordinary product times this smooth form. Local psh potentials p_i^j decrease to those of the given u, and 0<=p_i^j-p_i<=p_i^1-p_i, with locally integrable majorant, proves L1_loc convergence by dominated convergence. The positive source-potential rescaling in n1 preserves these hypotheses.

The measures mu_j=<T_uj^d>omega^(n-d) have uniform mass M_d on compact X. Every weak cluster point nu dominates mu_u by local lower semicontinuity and a nonnegative smooth partition of unity. Both have mass M_d. Thus nu-mu_u is positive with zero mass and vanishes. All cluster points coincide, proving convergence of the entire sequence. The same proof handles any decreasing sequence in the more-singular full-mass domain whose limit has full mass, and other decreasing bounded-type majorants in that domain. For d=0 the operator is identically omega^n and the conclusion is immediate.

A bounded-equivalent anchor change preserves dominance up to constants, d and M_d, hence this operator domain. Changing omega within its class preserves the full-mass condition by closedness of <T_u^d>, although it can change the measure. No invariance under arbitrary auxiliary-class change is asserted. For unbounded u, retained singularity data are its actual current and a dominating reference bounded type; equality of its bounded type to [psi] is not required.

For d>=1, investigate the full-mass domain with sum_{a=0}^d integral|u-psi|<T_u^aP^(d-a)>omega^(n-d)<infinity. With u<=psi, Vu arXiv:2005.13241v3 Section3 applies with m=d, P_j=P, smooth relative current R=omega^(n-d) and linear weight chi(t)=t. In our potential convention its joint energy is d sum_a C(d,a)integral(psi-u)<T_u^aP^(d-a)>omega^(n-d). Vu's literal source potentials u/2,psi/2 give half this expression; multiplication by two is the explicit linear-weight homogeneity conversion. Finiteness is equivalent because all finitely many summands are nonnegative. Top-degree cohomology equality is mass equality on connected compact oriented X. Vu Theorem3.4 supplies convexity, and Corollary3.2 supplies bounded-equivalent-anchor invariance of finiteness. Their printed proofs invoke prior literature and are accepted as scoped standard foundations, not reconstructed new lemmas. The operator continuity proved above applies to this domain and the larger full-mass domain.

This includes genuinely unbounded differences. Take X=P1_y x P1_z, normalized Fubini–Study forms eta_y,eta_z, theta=eta_y, psi=0 and omega=eta_y+eta_z. Then d=1 and M_1=1. Near y=0 set f(y)=-(-log|y|)^a, 0<a<1/2, extend with a smooth cutoff on an annulus, multiply by sufficiently small c>0 and subtract a constant. On the annulus the lower Hessian bound is finite, while near zero its radial second derivative is a(1-a)(-t)^(a-2)>0 for t=log|y|. Hence eta_y+ddc(cf)>=0. The radial slope ca(-t)^(a-1) tends to zero, so this current has no atom at zero. Stokes gives total mass1, which is also its nonpluripolar mass. Pull back u=cf to X. The smooth-volume linear-weight integral is finite by exponential radial area; the current-weighted integral is controlled by integral_infinity s^(2a-2)ds, finite for a<1/2. Thus u lies in the joint finite-energy domain but u-psi is unbounded.

The general finite-energy route remains unfinished. Weak convergence does not justify multiplication by unbounded weights. No uniform weighted-tail estimate, equality and continuity of truncated energy values, unbounded numerical cocycle or general unbounded reference-change theorem is proved. Degree-d joint finiteness has not here been shown to control weighted degrees k<d in the positive-epsilon expansion or a joint truncation/epsilon limit. The bounded o(epsilon) norm estimate cannot simply be transferred to arbitrary unbounded differences. These are unresolved proof steps, not counterexamples.

Full proof and literal supporting source bodies are in P15.2-argument.md, Sections2 and9. Rerun: python build.py. Original P15.2 remains open.

A divisorial reference in the same class has d=0, although the nef class numerical dimension is1. notes.text:
This note uses n1's operator and degree results and n2's limited unbounded extension. It gives analytic limitations and reproducibility evidence, not a complete solution or universal impossibility theorem.

Let X=P1_y x P1_z, theta=eta_y, psi=u=0, omega=eta_y+eta_z, with normalized Fubini–Study forms. The class alpha=[eta_y] is nef, alpha^2=0 and alpha[omega]>0. BEGZ Definition1.17 identifies positive products of nef classes with cup products, so vol(alpha)=0. The smooth actual reference has d=1, M_1=1 and mu=eta_y eta_z. For nonconstant smooth real g(z), choose small nonzero t with eta_z+t ddc g>0. The cohomologous Kähler form omega'=omega+t ddc g gives mu'-mu=t eta_y ddc g !=0. Indeed ddc g cannot vanish for nonconstant g on compact P1, by the maximum principle, and its nonzero local coefficient remains nonzero after wedging the other factor's positive area form. Both masses equal1. Thus this actual measure on X needs the full form even after class and mass are fixed. Scaling omega by c scales mass and energy by c^(n-d). This proves necessity for this construction, not a characterization of minimum data for every conceivable theory.

In the same class take D={y=0}xP1 and the logarithmic reference T_psi=[D]. Our convention gives ddc log|s|_h^2=[D]-theta: locally ddc log|z|^2=delta_0 because log r^2 has outward flux4pi and ddc acts as Delta/(4pi) times area; subtracting the metric weight supplies curvature. The current vanishes off D, and nonpluripolar products omit D, so <T_psi>=0 and its actual degree is d=0. The class numerical dimension is1 by alpha[omega]>0 and alpha^2=0. Hence actual-type degree need not equal numerical dimension. In degree0 the operator is omega^n; it retains type in its domain but does not distinguish potentials by its output. A degree(d,d) current on X does not itself produce a geometric d-dimensional quotient.

Relative to the unchanged catalogue, n1 removes the supplied-fibration hypothesis on its specified bounded actual-type domain, and n2 adds a full-mass operator with decreasing continuity. They leave minimum-reference characterization, an intrinsic lower-dimensional carrier, arbitrary perturbation-choice independence and a general unbounded finite-energy/cocycle/path theory unresolved. No supplied mixed-volume verdict, source-prose assertion or other worker's result is used. No priority claim is made. Status is partial and candidate=false.
